candidates.raw_excerpt: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. candidates.raw_excerpt: On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). On 26 November, following 26 hours of negotiations in Mannheim, IG Metall announced that it had reached an agreement with employers’ associations. candidates.title: US approves SpaceX plan for 1 million space data center satellites
candidates.raw_excerpt:
The US government on Wednesday granted SpaceX approval to deploy 1 million satellites, allowing the company to operate artificial intelligence data centers in space.

The SpaceX constellation, called "Starmind," includes up to 1 million solar-powered data center satellites designed to run AI workloads in orbit and beam the results back to Earth.

SpaceX must deploy and operate one authorized space station in its assigned orbit by November 25, 2033, while the remaining satellites must be launched and operational by November 25, 2040, according to an order issued by the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

Proponents of orbital data centers say that harnessing solar energy would ease pressure on power grids and reduce the use of other resources, such as water, on Earth. Opponents, however, warn of risks including atmospheric pollution and in-orbit collisions that could affect other essential satellites.

Since SpaceX filed its application with the FCC in January, the agency said it had received "a substantial number" of public comments, including petitions to deny the application filed by several major satellite companies and the American Astronomical Society (AAS).

The AAS said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the FCC's decision, adding that "the proposed constellation would significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities and the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky."

candidates.raw_excerpt: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed as orbital data centers for artificial intelligence computing. The order, released by the FCC’s Space Bureau on November 25, marks the first U.S. authorization of its kind. It sets a 14-year window for SpaceX to place the full network in low Earth orbit. If fully built, Starmind would dwarf every satellite launched in the history of spaceflight. According to Jonathan McDowell’s catalog dated November 18, roughly 28,800 satellites have been placed in orbit since Sputnik in 1957. About 17,200 remain active . Of those, more than 11,100 are Starlink spacecraft. That means SpaceX already operates roughly two-thirds of all active satellites and more than a third of every satellite ever launched . Starmind would multiply that scale by nearly two orders of magnitude. The first-generation satellite, designated AI1, is substantially larger than current Starlink vehicles. With solar arrays and radiators deployed, the spacecraft is designed to span roughly 70 meters in one axis and 20 meters in the other. The FCC approved six orbital shells between approximately 500 and 1,002 kilometers altitude. Three shells sit at inclinations of around 26 to 32 degrees, while the other three are in sun-synchronous orbits between roughly 97 and 99 degrees. candidates.title: Sustainable mobility in a changing world
candidates.raw_excerpt:
Transport shapes how people live, work and trade. As cities grow and international commerce expands, making travel cleaner, more efficient and accessible to everyone has become an urgent global priority.

November 26 marks World Sustainable Transport Day, a UN initiative promoting safer, greener and better connected transport. The day carries added meaning in 2026, the first year of the UN Decade of Sustainable Transport (2026-2035).

In cities, replacing gas-guzzling cars with electric ones is just one step towards greener daily journeys. To truly reduce car dependence, commuters need reliable public transit, safe cycling routes and seamless links between different modes of transport.

In Beijing, a city pilot lets riders bring bicycles onto select subway lines to link cycling with rail travel, while a 14-kilometer greenway along the Grand Canal in Tongzhou District offers a corridor for cycling and walking.

Similar efforts are also underway in other parts of the world. In Denmark's capital Copenhagen, the city aims for at least 75% of all trips to be made on foot, by bicycle or by public transport.

Its network allows passengers to combine cycling with metro, train and bus services, making low-carbon travel a more practical everyday choice.

candidates.title: Nepal and UN roll out $49.94m flood defense for Himalayan communities
candidates.raw_excerpt:
The Nepali government, in collaboration with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), launched a project worth $49.94 million on Wednesday to protect vulnerable Himalayan communities from glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs).

Work on the GLOF-Sanjibani Project will lower water levels in four high-altitude glacial lakes: Thulagi Lake, Lumding Tsho, Hongu 2 and Lower Barun, by 2033. It will also upgrade early warning systems and monitoring while building natural and structural defenses to reduce downstream flood risks in the watersheds. 

Senior government officials, Green Climate Fund and UNDP representatives, local authorities, technical experts and development partners attended the launch in Nepal's capital Kathmandu. 

It comes in the wake of the catastrophic flash floods that struck Nepal on August 26, triggered by a high-altitude glacial and rock collapse. The disaster killed at least 1,403 people and left 6,150 others missing.

Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, of the Shenzhou 24 crew entered the China Space Station on Wednesday. Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board the space station.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Wednesday that China is ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to deepen international cooperation in space, improve global governance of outer space, and ensure that the benefits of space exploration are shared more broadly by all humanity.

"We are ready to deepen exchanges and cooperation with more countries and regions in areas such as joint astronaut selection and training, scientific experiments and more," Zhou Yaqiang, chief systems designer of the General Technology Department of the China Manned Space Agency, told CGTN.

The China Space Station has abundant resources for scientific experiments, stable in-orbit operational capabilities, a mature space transportation system for travel to and from the station, and a well-established astronaut selection and training system. The country is also advancing its lunar exploration program according to plan. 

"Together, we can promote the rapid development of space technology, explore the vast universe, and benefit all humanity," Zhou said.
